title: Winter sun from Manchester in January: 10 direct flights compared
author: Brogan
intro: In January, the warmest places you can fly to direct from Manchester are the Canaries, Madeira, Morocco, the Red Sea and Cape Verde, all between about 4 and 6½ hours away. Here's how they compare for warmth, flight time and what you'll actually do there.
seo_title: Winter sun from Manchester in January: 4-6 hrs away
seo_description: The Canaries are about 4 hours from Manchester and 20-22°C in January. Egypt and Cape Verde are warmer but further. 10 direct options compared.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Warm and close:** the Canaries, about 4 hrs
- **Warmest:** Cape Verde, about 25°C
- **Best for sea and reefs:** the Red Sea
- **Same time as the UK:** Canaries, Madeira

The temperatures here are average daytime highs for January, from the climate figures in our guides. Flight times are typical direct times from Manchester. Routes and airlines were checked in October 2026 and change every season, so check the airline's timetable before you book.

Cyprus is often sold as winter sun too, but [Paphos](/destinations/paphos) averages about 17°C in January, which is pleasant for walking but not reliable beach weather.

sections.heading: The Canaries: the easy choice
sections.text:
The four big Canary Islands are the default January escape from Manchester for good reason. Jet2, easyJet, TUI and Ryanair all fly there, the flights are about four hours, and there's no time difference, so nobody's body clock suffers.

They're not all the same, though:

- **Tenerife and Gran Canaria** are the warmest of the four, with the most to do, from Mount Teide to Las Palmas old town. Stay in the south for the best sunshine.
- **Lanzarote** is quieter and lower, with volcanic scenery and César Manrique's art. Our [Lanzarote or Fuerteventura](/blog/lanzarote-or-fuerteventura) post compares it with its neighbour.
- **Fuerteventura** has the longest, emptiest beaches, but the wind can make January days feel cooler.

The sea is cool in January, around 19°C, so a heated pool is worth checking for if you want to swim.

sections.heading: Madeira and Morocco: warm, not hot
sections.text:
[Madeira](/destinations/madeira) is a little cooler, at about 19°C, but greener and better for walking, with levada paths, gardens and Funchal's old town. easyJet and Jet2 fly there from Manchester. The approach into Funchal is one of Europe's most dramatic, and our post on [which side of the plane to sit on flying to Madeira](/blog/which-side-of-the-plane-to-sit-on-flying-to-madeira) explains the best seats.

Morocco is just an hour ahead. [Agadir](/destinations/agadir) is a beach resort with a long sandy bay, about 20°C in January, and Jet2 flies there all year. [Marrakech](/destinations/marrakech) is a city, not a beach, at about 18°C by day but cold at night, so pack a jumper.

Tip: in January, Marrakech works best as a three- or four-night break, while Agadir suits a week of easy sunshine. Our [Marrakech in 3 days](/blog/marrakech-in-3-days) post has a plan.

sections.heading: The Red Sea and Cape Verde: warmer, further
sections.text:
If you want to be properly warm, you need to go further. [Hurghada](/destinations/hurghada) and [Sharm el-Sheikh](/destinations/sharm-el-sheikh) on Egypt's Red Sea are about 21 to 22°C in January, with sunshine almost every day and coral reefs just offshore. The flight is about 5½ hours.

TUI flies to both from Manchester in winter, and easyJet serves Hurghada. Jet2 is returning to Egypt from February 2027, so it won't help for a January trip this winter.

[Cape Verde](/destinations/cape-verde) is the warmest of the lot at about 25°C, with long white beaches on Sal and Boa Vista. The flight is about six hours, and TUI and easyJet fly there.

Watch out: UK visitors need a visa for Egypt, and Cape Verde has its own pre-arrival rules. Check the entry requirements on GOV.UK before you book.

sections.heading: Which to choose
sections.text:
- **For a short break of three or four nights:** Madeira, Marrakech or the nearest Canary Island to you on the timetable.
- **For a beach week with no jet lag:** Tenerife, Gran Canaria or Lanzarote.
- **For snorkelling and guaranteed warmth:** Hurghada or Sharm el-Sheikh.
- **For the warmest beach weather:** Cape Verde.
- **For walking rather than lying on a beach:** Madeira.

Our post on [winter sun with no jet lag](/blog/winter-sun-with-no-jet-lag) covers the places on or near UK time in more detail.

sections.heading: When in January to go
sections.text:
- **The first week:** still part of the Christmas holidays, so flights and hotels are at peak prices until the schools go back.
- **From the second week:** prices usually drop sharply and stay low until the February half term.
- **Daylight:** in the Canaries, the sun sets at about 6pm UK time, against about 4pm in Manchester.
- **Early flights:** our guide to [how early to arrive at Manchester Airport](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-manchester-airport) has the timings by terminal.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Manchester?
sections.text:
Start with the [Canaries](/destinations/tenerife) for an easy week, or [Cape Verde](/destinations/cape-verde) if you want real heat. The [where to go in January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january) page has ideas beyond winter sun, and our guide to [where you can fly direct from Manchester](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-manchester-airport) lists the full route map.

Can't agree between the islands and the Red Sea? Read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or put each option into a draw and let it decide.

faqs.question: Where is hottest in January with a direct flight from Manchester?
faqs.answer: Cape Verde, at about 25°C, is the warmest. Egypt's Red Sea resorts are about 21 to 22°C. Tenerife and Gran Canaria are the warmest of the closer options at about 22°C.

faqs.question: How long is the flight from Manchester to Tenerife?
faqs.answer: About four hours and 15 minutes, depending on the wind. There's no time difference between the Canaries and the UK.

faqs.question: Is Marrakech warm in January?
faqs.answer: Warm by day, at about 18°C, but chilly at night, when it often drops to about 6°C. It's better for a city break than a beach holiday in January.

faqs.question: Is Cyprus warm enough in January?
faqs.answer: Not for the beach. Paphos averages about 17°C in January, which is pleasant for walking and sightseeing, but the sea is cool.
